corrections.text: The summary says 'LWN, The Register, Phoronix and project documents show Rust warned in the compiler and scanned public crates, Python chose an opt-in warning, and Git guards planned breaks with a build switch.' Only LWN (the Rust warning and crater scan) and project documents (PEP 686 and Python's io documentation for the opt-in EncodingWarning; Git's BreakingChanges document for the WITH_BREAKING_CHANGES switch) state those mechanisms. The Register and Phoronix, as cited, report the Python 3.15, Rust 1.100 and Git releases and timelines but do not mention the warnings or the build switch.

The article calls the LWN addition on Git 2.98, 2.99 and 3.0 'an undated update'. The update carries no date in the article text, but LWN's editor says in a comment on the same page (Sep 22, 2026, 16:04 UTC) that he added it, so it postdates the September 18 article. The BreakingChanges document, read on November 13, was therefore checked later than the update and still says there is no planned release date.

The article lists 'When GitHub will support SHA-256 repositories' as unsettled, citing LWN's September 18 statement that this is unclear. A reader comment on the same LWN page (Sep 18, 2026) points to a SHA-256 repository hosted on GitHub (github.com/bk2204/talk-rust-in-git), and the Herald's check on November 13 found that repository's object IDs are 64 hexadecimal characters. No cited source says whether GitHub offers SHA-256 repositories generally, so the question of general support remains as LWN left it.
